To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we were able to model the light-scattering spectra from a real OPC with a T-matrix model, and we were able to derive the light-scattering properties of model particles from a TEM sample with a new algorithm.

the OPC signal is a function of the size and shape of the particles, the OPC can be modeled with a T-matrix code and the model can be applied to retrieve information on the absorption properties of particles.

(1) the OPC response to a given aerosol can be modeled with good precision, (2) the OPC can be used to retrieve the absorption properties of aerosol particles, (3) the OPC is a promising tool in aerosol research for the characterization of aerosol particles in terms of their size, shape, and refractive index.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a new methodology for deriving more than just the aerosol size distributions with optical particle counters (OPCs) by combining OPC data with results of transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and optical models.
the development of a new methodology for the retrieval of aerosol absorption properties from optical particle counter measurements.
the modeling of the light-scattering signals from an optical particle counter to retrieve the absorption properties of the particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

OPCs can be used to derive information on the light absorption properties of atmospheric aerosol particles, provided that the OPC is equipped with state-of-the-art signal-processing electronics and that the particle populations are sufficiently diverse.
a T-matrix model of light scattering from nonspherical particles is a powerful tool for analyzing light-scattering data of OPCs.
the OPC is a useful tool for the study of aerosol properties and composition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the OPC can be used to derive the absorption properties of atmospheric particles.

the OPC is an instrument that is capable of detecting and characterizing aerosol particles with a wide range of sizes and shapes, provided that the pulse height is resolved in a sufficiently high resolution.
a new methodology has been developed for the analysis of OPC signals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the OPC is a very useful tool for aerosol research.
the OPC can be used as a tool to derive aerosol optical properties.

OPC measurements of the scattered light pulses are sensitive to the morphology of the particles and that the OPC can be used to distinguish between different morphological types of atmospheric particles.
